candidate_clusters.title: SZK versus counting upper bounds
candidate_clusters.verdict: No ordinary inclusion found. HVPZK⊆PP concerns perfect simulation; SZK permits statistical error. The promise gap in Volkovich is tied to the resulting sampler input length, so ordinary polarization cannot simply be substituted.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: PP=PostBQP is insufficient: replacing an entire multi-message statistical protocol by one postselection computation is an additional theorem. The paper supplies only an oracle obstruction to such a relativizing transformation.

candidate_clusters.title: SBP versus GapP approximation and exact normalizers
candidate_clusters.verdict: SBP⊆PP is already known. No stronger roster upper bound found. A #P acceptance gap with an unrestricted upper tail cannot be substituted for the bounded interval required by AWPP.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: WAPP is an auxiliary class with an upper bound on its counting function; WAPP⊆SBP and WAPP⊆AWPP do not imply SBP⊆AWPP.

candidate_clusters.title: SBP and SZK versus quantum witnesses
candidate_clusters.verdict: All four remain candidates. Both cited papers explicitly work with oracles for their negative results.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: SBQP/A0PP contains QMA and SBP but is not QMA; dropping this distinction would create false inclusions.

candidate_clusters.title: Zero-error and bounded-error randomness versus exact counting
candidate_clusters.verdict: Current ZPP⊆CeqP, ZPP⊆AWPP, and BQP⊆AWPP labels are supported. No ZPP⊆WPP or ZPP⊆parityP theorem found; each has a direct oracle barrier.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: A Las Vegas algorithm may have variable failure probability. Its successful branch count is not thereby an FP normalizer or a unique witness.

candidate_clusters.title: NP∩coNP versus exact-counting and unambiguous intersections
candidate_clusters.verdict: NP∩coNP⊆CeqP already follows from coNP⊆CeqP. No stronger counting inclusion found. Theorem8 of MN16 starts from UP∩coUP, a smaller intersection.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: Since ZPP⊆NP∩coNP relativizes, STT and BBF barriers also rule out relativizing inclusions of this intersection in WPP and parityP. They do not prove ordinary noninclusions.

candidate_clusters.title: Complementary unambiguity and zero knowledge
candidate_clusters.verdict: No new status found. coUP⊆SPP/LWPP/WPP/AWPP/parityP/PP follows from UP⊆SPP and complement closure; it does not follow that coUP⊆NP.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: The first Menda–Watrous oracle witness lies in both UP and coUP and outside QSZK. It prevents a generic relativizing zero-knowledge simulation of either unambiguous class.

candidate_clusters.title: Exact and approximate counting versus BQP and quantum proofs
candidate_clusters.verdict: QMA/coQMA/QCMA⊆PP and BQP⊆AWPP are already present. WPP⊆postBQP_FP is an upper bound using postselection, not WPP⊆BQP.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: The exact postselection identities use a fixed gate set. No gate-independent exact equivalence was introduced into the benchmark.

candidate_clusters.title: Polynomial hierarchy and proof classes versus counting
candidate_clusters.verdict: No omitted unconditional endpoint found. Θ2P⊆PP is already known; P^NP, a full adaptive-oracle class, cannot be replaced by its logarithmic-query restriction.
candidate_clusters.scope_check: Randomized reductions, P^PP/P^#P upper bounds, nonzero-measure hypotheses, and relativized worlds do not resolve the ordinary candidate pairs.

residual_risk.rationale: The inspected older source chains cover several plausible high-fanout shortcuts and independently confirm that the tempting claims use different models. This warrants a modest downward revision, not multiplying independent no-finding probabilities: sources share ancestry, no omission-detection rate is calibrated, and141 of the broader526 candidate interfaces lie outside the exact counting-by-other slice. The mean fanout remains6 because an unnoticed nonrelativizing or intermediate-class result could still propagate to several labels.
